title: A copy follows the original when its look changes, not just its shape
goal: Today, changing a component's own fade, blur, shadow or rounded corners does not reach the copies you have placed, even though moving a piece inside it does. Make the whole look follow, without the copy's own sliders snapping back under your hand.
notes: Step C5 left this out on purpose: the sync manages a copy's children, isFrame, clipsContents, backgroundHex and size, but NOT Layer.style, because syncing style would revert an Effects slider dragged on a copy. The honest fix is the override model from C6: style becomes an overridable property, so an untouched copy follows and a touched one does not. Sequence it after C6 (docs/design/ui-building.md, step 6) rather than before.
acceptance: Changing opacity, blur, shadow or corner radius on the original changes every copy
A copy you have styled yourself keeps what you set, and says so
The notice counts these edits the same way it counts a change to the contents
Covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Whole-look vs part-by-part: taking the copy's whole look the moment one slider moves would mean a copy that was faded once never gets the original's new shadow. Part by part is what a person expects and is barely more work, so the look follows field by field. (2) How does the app tell a person's edit from the sync's own writing? Not by marking the edit site (every future style path would have to remember, and one that forgot would silently snap back), but by remembering on the copy the original's look as of the last time it was put in step. Anything that differs from that is the copy's own. Automatic, and undo-safe because it is all one snapshot. (3) 'Says so' has to be where the person just dragged, not only in the Component section: a revert arrow appears on the Effects/Shadow row itself, plus one summary row on the copy's section for when Effects is scrolled away. (4) Old documents: a copy with no remembered look adopts the original's current one, so nothing on screen changes on open and a copy that was already styled keeps what it had.

A copy now follows its original's fade, blur, corner radius, border and shadow, part by part: a copy you styled keeps what you set, says which parts are its own on both the Effects row and its Component section, and has a way back. Model in PhotonzCore/ComponentStyle.swift + the sync in ComponentInstances.swift (19 tests written first, 2001 green); verified live in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/component-look-walk.json. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-component-look.json with two real captures.
